newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mixed, hedging versus corn gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mixed, hedging versus corn gains.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed with late hedge pressure partly offset by a turn higher in the corn pit which triggered short covering in wheat, traders said.
"They had gotten a little short and corn started coming back so they bought it (wheat shorts) back," a trader said referring to the late firming trend in wheat futures.
The corn and soybean market remained dominated by dry weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest which was threatening to cut yield potential for the 1997 U.S. corn/soy crop.
Wheat this week persisted in following the gains in corn and soybeans but ongoing hedge pressure and short term overbought technical signals continued to cap rallies.
"There's pretty good hedging in wheat and everything else today. Funds keep buying it but there was quite a lot of farm movement," a trader said.
The U.S. marketing pipeline remains full of healthy, new crop winter wheat as the harvesting of an abundant supply winds down.
Wheat closed 1/2 cent per bushel lower to 4-1/2 cents higher, with September down 1/2 at $3.61-1/2 per bushel.

Term Commodities and FIMAT Futures each bought one half million bushels of December, traders said. Cargill Inc, E.D. and F. Man Interntional and SAK Futures bought and sold one half million bushels of December, traders said. Prudential Securities sold one million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread trading, Prudential Securities did five million bushels of March/December at 9-/2 to 11 cents, premium March, traders said.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 September $3.50 puts at five cents and sold 400 September $3.40 puts at 2-1/4 cents, traders said. Prudential Securities bought 200 December $3.80 calls at 18-1/2 to 19 cents, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 20,000 contracts, compared with Thursday's actual volume of 26,359. Options volume was pegged at 7,000 contracts, against Thursday's 5,692 contracts.
